I previously took this course with a different instructor who taught exclusively in the Spring semester. Unfortunately, that experience was far from ideal, marked by a lack of communication and blatantly solving models without providing any intuition or underlying explanation at all. 

In contrast, Professor Lee's teaching style was simply a breath of fresh air. As an elite researcher in his field, he possesses an extensive knowledge base. To be honest, his e-mails and first few lectures can be a bit intimidating, but please don't be misled: because Professor Lee is an incredibly approachable and extremely kind instructor whose primary aim is to make us world-class economists.

If we look at his teaching philosophy, it is deeply rooted in understanding. Although we solve models, his teaching is definitely beyond that of mechanically solving models; he emphasizes grasping the core concepts and intuitions behind each economic model. After taking this course, I will probably not remember the models and the way we solved them, but amazingly enough, Professor Lee taught this course in such a way that I will never forget the main takeaways and intuition behind all the models; it's just incredible.

So, choosing Professor Lee's course has been a decision I'm profoundly grateful for. Despite the potential for delaying graduation, I would strongly advise against taking this course with the other instructor who only teaches in the Spring semester because the lack of understanding and retention from that experience simply isn't worth it. 

With Professor Lee, you're not just learning; you're gaining invaluable insights that stay with you. So, I strongly recommend taking this course from Professor Lee.
